utterances.text: The interpreters disagree. Go ahead, Mr. Pisarevic. It was a gun. I don't think -- because he is just describing -- anyway, you go ahead with your cross-examination and see whether or not the type will actually matter in which case you'll have to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, you've served the army, the JNA army.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what type of weapon was shown to you by your neighbour Slobodan Kukrika?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was serving the army, this type of weaponry didn't exist, that type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you mentioned to the Trial Chamber that it was a submachine-gun 84, light machine-gun 84.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that machine-gun by its dimensions bigger than other infantry weapons like rifles, the calibre?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The calibre is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness stated -- first he answered "Yes, but the calibre is different." So the question was about the size of the weapon, and he answered yes, it has a bigger size.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the answer, the one for the line 24 where he says "the calibre is the same." Are you saying the answer, it isn't correctly recorded?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. This part of the answer is correct, but first he says "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is the same question that you are looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's line 22. First it is the question of the dimension of this weapon, and then the calibre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we can clear that by the question being repeated, and then the witness can answer. And I think there's a slight problem -- the slight problem we are having is there's overlapping. So the witness should wait, pause a minute after counsel has completed asking the question to allow interpretation of his question to be completed, and then you start answering, and then your answer will also be interpreted at the right time and it will be completed. Because when there's overlapping, then we have problems with the record of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry about this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This weapon, this light machine-gun that was shown to you by Slobodan Kukrika, was it in terms of size larger than traditional infantry weapons such as automatic rifles and others?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on which automatic rifle. Do you mean Kalashnikov or what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The automatic rifles which were standard weapons for the Yugoslav People's Army produced by Zastava factory?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was larger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kukrika tell you on that occasion that he was a member of the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he tell you that the weapon in question was received by him in his capacity of member of the Yugoslav People's Army and the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Mustafa Omeranovic, also a neighbour of yours, was a commander of the platoon in the 4th Detachment of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned another neighbour nicknamed Came?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that this person is, in fact, Cazim Atic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is. I don't know his first name but his last name was Atic. He lived in the third house away from mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he the one that told you that he was a member of the 4th Detachment and that he got his weapon from the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about Tota. That is, in fact, Nizam Ramusovic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know[redacted]?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do regrettably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He is a Muslim, isn't he,[redacted]?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that he was one of the managing directors in the Mebos company where you used to work?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a director.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he one of the managerial staff?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he, too, was a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Nasir Ramusovic,[redacted]?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was one of the commanders in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will stay for a while on the events prior to the 17th of April, 1992. You are aware that in the town of Samac, various sabotage actions took place in the town?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are also aware of the events that occurred in the course of 1992 such as the killing of two Muslim young men by a bomb that exploded in the Valentino cafe?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned in your testimony that you happened to be on the spot, on the corner of Vuk Karadzic Street when shooting occurred, the shooting was directed at the vehicle driven by Mersad Mesic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't on the spot. It was further up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you arrived on the spot, did Mersad Mesic, Nizam Ramusovic, and Danilo Vitomir wear civilian clothes or military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mersad was in civilian clothes and Tota was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Danilo Vitomir dressed?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see him very well. He was turned away from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Nizam Ramusovic, nicknamed Tota, have a full of set of military uniform, or was he wearing just a military shirt?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a jacket. Only his footwear was military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see on that occasion, while you were on the spot, that they were armed?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer this: What kind of weapon did Mersad Mesic carry?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tota had a Kalashnikov, and I don't remember about Mersad. I can't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you are saying that Tota, that is Nizam Ramusovic, was carrying a Kalashnikov? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that weapons of the Kalashnikov type was never part of the weaponry of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I did see it in wartime, and I saw it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said on that occasion that on that day, you saw inside the vehicle those people driving and shooting, meaning Mersad Mesic, Nizam Ramusovic, and Danilo Vitomir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did you see them just once or several times?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three times. I saw them passing by my street, along my street, three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that Safet, a policeman, came out into the street in front of them and riddled their vehicle with bullets?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that this Safet Srna was a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also hear on that occasion that he was accompanied by another reserve policeman Adis Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we agree that this event took place on the 2nd of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the date. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Safet Srna and Adis Izetbegovic are both Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are Muslims both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that event, did you happen to see in town Safet Srna and Adis Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you, perhaps, hear that they had escaped to the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that near the house of Mujaga Omeranovic you had seen two trucks?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell me if those were civilian or military trucks?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, after I was examined, my memory returned to me and I can say that those were trucks from the separation company, meaning civilian trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about the persons who unloaded that case? Were they wearing uniforms or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Mustafa Omeranovic and Mr. Zaric, who you came -- you saw, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zaric was wearing trousers, and Mujaga Omeranovic had a sweater on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass close by them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was just in the same street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That spot where you were passing by, was it well-lit?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rather well-lit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what sort of jacket was Mr. Zaric wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then on good terms with Mr. Omeranovic and Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On pretty good terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you greet them? Did you say anything when you were passing by, as "hello"?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The house of Mr. Omeranovic, is it close to the piazza in Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a frequent normal occurrence for those trucks to bring goods to that marketplace and to stay parked there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will now move to the period after the 17th of April, 1992. And I have a couple of questions here. If I understood you correctly, you said that all Muslims and Croats had the obligation to report or get registered at the headquarters of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were informed so by Subasic and other couriers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a publicly proclaimed summons, a call-up, broadcast on Radio Samac that all persons should report to the Territorial Defence staff?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at least I didn't hear anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were registered at the Territorial Defence headquarters, did nobody tell you that you should report to the Buducnost company?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear the publicly broadcast call-up for all members of Territorial Defence, or rather all persons registered in the Territorial Defence to report to the courtyard of the Buducnost company?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got there, when did you arrive at the Buducnost company?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My son and I went there when we were asked to do so by Subasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you and your son got there, to the courtyard of the Buducnost company, you found there a certain number of members of the JNA, too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see on that occasion Jovo Savic, an officer, a reserve officer, rather?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. At least, I don't know by name. I don't recall who Jovo Savic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the name Jovica in your testimony? This Jovica had a house behind Trivo Lukic's house.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that this person is Jovo Savic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That first name and last name tell me nothing, but I know the nickname Jovica and he lived three houses away from me. I don't know him by full name. I know the person. I know he lives there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any persons, together with him, who were wearing the JNA uniform?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to those two, were there any others?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, but I didn't look closely. I was watching my son, and I was watching my own arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On all those members of the Yugoslav People's Army, did you see right next to the epaulet on the left arm a white rag, like an armband?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at that time, did you sometimes see on soldiers any armbands or rags on the sleeve?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, but they were red. Not rags really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean armbands?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something on the arm, like a decoration or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, are e talking about an armband which would be worn on the arm, or are we talking about a ribbon attached to an epaulet, because the two seem very different and we have already heard from this witness that the non-Serb population would be made to wear white armbands. So I think we want to be clear about an armband and something attached to the epaulet, like a ribbon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked about those people who were wearing military uniforms in specific. Those people were wearing those ribbons behind the epaulet, but a large number of members of the 4th Detachment did not wear any uniform. So on their sweaters or whatever they were wearing, they wore those bands on the sleeve. And some witnesses have already confirmed this. But since Mr. Hadzijusufovic has been questioned as to military personnel, I didn't want to ask any specific questions about the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you had been to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you had been to Dubica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, this Dubica that you had visited, is it a Serbian village?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have been to both places named Dubica, both Croatian and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have been to both Croatian Dubica and Serbian Dubica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You answered that you spent some time with a person in Dubica working for him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the Serbian or Croatian Dubica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was with Stevo Rundo in Serbian Dubica. It was right across the street from the Serbian church. His house was there, right across the street from the Serbian church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to that Dubica, Serbian Dubica, were many houses burned down?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the property of these people taken away or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Trnjak?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went passed through it prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war, you were not in the village of Trnjak during the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that it is a Serbian village?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these houses in Serbian Dubica which were burned down belonged to Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also spoke about the fact that you and another person, Rakocevic, that you covered a roof, a structure for the roof?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you removed in Odzak or Croatian Dubica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Croatian Dubica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this construction material for the roof, you then moved it and put it up in Srpska -- in Serbian Dubica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, behind the house of Father Stevo, Stevo Rundo, there's another house, another building, and we placed it on the -- put it on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that house burned down and the roof burned down?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one we were placing it on no, but the house in front of it, yes, did burn down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the territory of Odzak where you were moving around, did you see Muslims and Croats living in their apartments or in their villages?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When leaving, when going and taking -- removing property from family homes, did the -- were the owners present there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, was that abandoned property?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He is asking the witness abandoned. Abandoned is a legal term that calls for legal judgment. If he wants to rephrase if, if he wants to say there was no one there. But abandoned is a legal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. In fact, the witness's opinion in this type of evidence is not what you should be asking for because this is a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honours, with the position you've stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the property question, the property that you were removing, that you were taking, was it usually most frequently given to refugees, and persons that had no property whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of Samac or Dubica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dubica.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did this only for Stevo Rundo. When I was in Dubica, I didn't drive for anybody else. I drove for him. I came in front of the retirement home, and a person in a military uniform waited for me. His name is Stevo, going under the nickname of Rundo. He lived in Ive Lole Ribara Street. He told me you're going with me to Dubica and help me and my father to repair our home. He placed us on a tractor, and the pontoon bridge, we went to Dubica. The first work we did for him, let me say that for Stevo, his father and mother, I had absolutely no problems. They said nothing offensive. I never felt that these people would be violent. It was said to me, I had to go there and work there. So we stayed there for five or six days, and we were bringing to him furniture and also equipment from Croatian Dubica to his house straight up there. And thus, in five or six days, we went with tractor, and then we crossed that bridge which was later toppled by high waters, and we stayed with him ten days. And then this other building, which was there without a roof, I said "how come"? He said there was -- a gas cylinder was placed in there and exploded. So therefore, we went to another building, and we moved that roof material. We stayed ten days, and we returned to Samac. And Rakocevic stayed in Samac. And I and Stevo via Odzak, we went to do some other work. I was loading on his trailer wood, firewood, and then we returned in the evenings. And this lasted for another five days. It lasted -- he was -- for a certain period of time, they said "That's enough for you. You have enough wood." And I never -- I didn't work for him any more. I had to do all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All that you were bringing in, driving, it was -- Stevo didn't find in his home when he came back?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. But what we did bring in was more than enough for three houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the fact that on the territory of Odzak, precisely people from Serbian Dubica, Novi Grad, which was also a Serb settlement, and Trnjak, that they were detained by the Croatian Defence Council, HVO?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they told me that when we were -- when they came through the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that these houses had been burned down at the moment when the HVO was withdrawing with its population to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it after the exchange. I had a friend from Dubica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, we are coming to an end. I would only like to ask you another single question: You've said that you've known my client Mr. Simo Zaric some 30 years?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree or do you agree that Mr. Zaric was a person who was respected in the town of Samac, that he never manifested national or nationalistic characteristics, traits, and that in principle, that he was a popular person among the townspeople of Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Trial Chamber. Thank you, Mr. Hadzijusufovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The transcript, I think, is wrong. It says "before the war".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that was the answer. The answer is "Yes, before the war." That is page 56, line 12, isn't it? Line 12. Mr. Weiner, that's the answer you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, and it had Mr. Pisarevic saying "before the war". Now it has disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I'm saying is the answer at page 56, line 12, I understood it to say "Yes, before the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I thought the witness said "before the war."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm saying, but the transcript has left out "before the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a clarification in this respect: The witness answered yes, and then when Mr. Pisarevic said thank you, he said "before the war," just as an addendum to his answer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But the complete answer is "Yes, before the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it to be but it wasn't said in a certain line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, there was a pause. Yes, agreed. Mr. Lukic. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. My name is Novak Lukic. I will carry on the cross-examination. I would like to clarify certain facts that you have been presenting to us during the examination-in-chief. First of all, I would like to clarify one matter. Your first discussion with prosecutors you had in the 1st of May, 1998, with the --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My family and friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak personally with the investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of whom you are thinking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Agnes Inderhaug and Dijana Barbaric?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I participated in that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else participated in that talk?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife and son. It was a discussion, a talk we had, of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel. If you look at the transcript, line 19 of page 57, the names you mentioned of the persons, the investigators of the Tribunal, are not recorded. Can you just repeat the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the minutes, this talk was held with investigator Agnes Inderhaug, and translator Dijana Barbaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, you did not sign the minutes or any statement?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an informative talk that a trial would take place in cooperation with a translator who didn't perform quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you signed at the time no written statement?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your arrival to The Hague and giving a statement, you had a talk with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, the Prosecutor submitted this note to you which was carried out by the investigator, and you made your comments and they made addendas?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can agree that this statement had been read to you prior to your testimony.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stated that it's an informal discussion, and that it's an informal, nonvalid document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've given your comments, your corrections to this?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign the statement in front of -- to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave an oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign anything written when giving the statement to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement I gave to the Prosecutor, I made a solemn oath on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic? When exactly was this? Because it says after your arrival to The Hague on page 58, line 13. Is that this week, or is it on some other trip to The Hague? Maybe we could have a clarification on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I wanted to clarify, but probably I could clarify that better with the colleague Prosecutor. The Defence received two documents from the Prosecutor without dates but are statements of the witness concerning a statement he never made, he never signed. I wanted to know that we -- whether he signed anything or he just made an oath on this statement which he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure, okay. I was just going to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If we need your explanation -- unless Mr. Lukic wants an explanation from the Prosecutor. I thought those were questions the witness could answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he can. I would only like to hear whether the witness signed anything to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead with the witness. You can ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I shall ask the question. I assume that you stand after every statement you make, the oath is not a statement. I wanted to hear whether in the statement to the Prosecutor you've signed it or not.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I said that with the lawyer that I fully agree with what has been presented to me. Now, this is on my last trip, my last arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Prosecutor presented to you this note which he made in connection with the talks -- the interview he had with you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the last occasion when I arrived here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree with the -- we can agree with your statements contained in this written interview that you have made with the Prosecutor this most recent time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have to raise this question because this statement hasn't been signed, and we want to know behind which statements you stand. That is why we have to ask this question. At the beginning of the statement, you said you were from an old family from Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My impression was, and I would like to ask you in connection with that, whether you knew well your neighbours, the inhabitants of Sana?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who interested me, I knew them well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection in your statement -- answer to colleague Pisarevic and in your statement yesterday that you knew everybody, all members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew them personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew many inhabitants of Sana at the time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that even today, you have in your memory the faces and the names of those people who interested you, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement yesterday, you said that occasionally you went to the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understood it, it was after the end of the second shift, around 10.00 p.m., between 8.00 p.m. and 10.00 p.m. Could you be a bit more precise when occasionally?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe once a week or maybe two or three times in a row. But that would be just a single drink, and then I would leave. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Omer Nalic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally. I didn't go there often. Maybe I saw him once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Alija Futozovic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in the Cafe AS when you visited it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question, did you see him in the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Martin Benic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any one of the two in the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ivitsa Trgovac, going by the nickname of Koka, do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Koka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would also like to -- and what service did you -- what branch did you serve?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediate -- when were you relieved of military service, immediately after you served compulsory?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1988.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you up until then have your also plan and assignment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the reserve as sergeant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an officer in the reserve, you knew what it means not to respond to -- if you have a call-up?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described that on the 17th in the morning, you were also asked for identity papers in front of your house, and these people had the White Eagles insignia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also added that they asked you whether you had weapons in the house?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They asked for your ID?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't enter your home?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you're a Muslim, they only asked you whether you had weapons? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked whether somebody else came to us. There was a team, a group of people who went in front with two white flags, and the military went by the side. They came to me about an hour later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told these two people that nobody else turned up in my house prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they assign, did they note down any data in connection with the talk?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to question you about a search which hasn't come up in the talk with the Prosecutor. What do you know about the search of house of Hanka Secic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not a home. It was an apartment, and it's my mother. Two policemen came to her apartment at 1.00 a.m., searched the apartment. There was no electricity. They did that by candlelight. They searched the apartment, made also a report, a statement, and she had to sign that statement. They told her that they were looking for a radio transmitter, and they didn't put that on the paper. And I submitted that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now like to tender this document that the witness stated to the Prosecution and the Prosecution made available to us, and if this is admitted, I would like to ask a couple of more questions on this subject.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my mother. There's nothing to hide about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I wanted to find out about the statement you're talking about, is this the one which the Prosecutor and the investigators were writing down as they were discussing with the witness? Which one is this? Is it the statement of the witness, and we all know what a statement is, or is it the Prosecutors' notes or investigators' notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's neither. This is a record of the search of apartment and other premises drawn up by the Public Security Station of Samac, and the apartment in question belonged to the witness's mother. It's just a document made available by this witness to the OTP when he gave his interview, and it is evidence to the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right. You can show it to the witness first. It is translated, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it has an authorised translation attached to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be a good idea if the usher could put the B/C/S version on the ELMO so that the accused can see the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure that can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document I asked you about, and you replied that your mother provided it to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I would like to know about this document is this: On page 2, it's the third paragraph from the bottom, and it says: "At the request of the persons attending the search, the following is included in the record." Do you see what it says on the form?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mother tell you what she wrote down in the record? Because we can't really see it in any of the copies you provided.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't tell me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you that she wrote any remarks regarding the search?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It sufficed that they had come to her apartment in the middle of the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like for this document to be given a number for identification and to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Shall we have the number as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The English translation will be D31/ -- no, sorry. I apologise. D32/3. And B/C/S will be D32/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall we now take our break, because I'm going to move on to different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll take a break and resume at 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to move on to another topic. Yesterday, and earlier today, you described at some length your work during the time when you were under work obligation. In those seven months, did you come to the retirement home every day at 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Depending on what?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on where I worked, depending on whether there was shelling, depending on fuel. And when I would come back from one assignment, I would not report for one or two days afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your obligation was to come to the retirement home every day that you were in Samac at 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said yourself that there had been cases when you would fail to report for one or two days after a work assignment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people I worked for told me that I could not report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you punished in any way for not reporting?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody knew that I had come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after returning from work in the field where you had spent some time, you were not duty-bound to report to the retirement home immediately?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But still, you didn't do so, not every time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were not punished by anyone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't know. They didn't know I had come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you failed to report when necessary upon return from the field.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never strictly defined how long I would stay on a certain assignment in the field. And I did that after my children had left Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those times when you did report to the retirement home to go and work, was it at 6.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a couple of questions regarding the building of the retirement home. It had two floors?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many floors, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can we agree that the premises of the retirement home occupied the ground and the first floor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground floor, there was a retirement home in a big room. On the side, there was a small room. And upstairs, there were offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree, or rather do you know that before the war, the local community was also located on those premises?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was also a conference room?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was one on the right-hand side, but it wasn't big.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic. The translation on line 4 of page 68 talks about the local community was also located on those premises. I'm not sure that I understand what the "local community" means in that context. I wonder whether you might clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to explain, or shall I phrase it as a question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You'd better explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Well, either way, it might just be translation. In any event, either way, yourself or the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, I'll try to explain briefly. The local commune under the constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was the basic territorial unit in the administrative structure, but it did not have powers in itself; rather, it was part of the municipality which, as a territorial unit, had all the organs of local authority, the Court, the police, government, et cetera. So the local commune is a territorial unit in which, as the constitution put it, the citizens dealt with all their day-to-day affairs within the self-management system. And thus, in Samac, it was the same thing. There was -- there were local communes within the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. But I now understand it was because the word "local community" was there, and not the word commune, which I had an understanding of. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that in the Defence case, we will use expert testimony to clarify this concept and the real meaning of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the room occupied by Dzevad Celic was on the ground floor, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the work obligation was organised and managed by the Secretariat for Defence of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me get this clear: You don't know or the Defence Secretariat didn't manage it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, and it wasn't managed by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have to clarify this further. If you don't know, then how do you know it wasn't managed by the Secretariat of Defence?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is something wrong with my earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Would the usher please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I caused this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please explain, do you know that the Secretariat for National Defence did not manage the work obligation or you don't know about it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work obligation was managed from upstairs, from the second floor. There was no military person anywhere in the vicinity of the quarters where the work obligation was carried out. There were no officers or Secretariat for National Defence during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you used to be in the JNA earlier.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were demobilised, did you ever visit the Secretariat for National Defence of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was across the street from the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was everyone wearing uniforms there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority did, or perhaps half and half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the personnel of the Secretariat for National Defence did not necessarily wear uniforms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You just said that the premises of the Secretariat for National Defence were across the road from the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it necessarily the case that all the offices of a certain secretariat are located in one place?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Milos Bogdanovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this name. Perhaps if I saw a picture of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat for the benefit of the interpreters and reporters. The name was Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not get the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not from Samac. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Across the road from the SUP, was there a building belonging to the Territorial Defence as you said yesterday in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall we agree that the premises of the Territorial Defence did not include the Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reported there when I had to go to military duty, but I didn't go there on other occasions. I didn't need to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps that this secretariat was located in the vicinity of the old hotel?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which location you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the communications centre, if you know that building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about it. I never entered it. It was in the old bank, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I never went in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But still, you claim that the organisation of the work duty was handled on the upper floor above Dzevad Celic's office?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Bozo Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really know him, but I know the face. I used to see him when I went to the defence building. I don't know if I could recognise him now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show this witness Document D22/F ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, will you be so kind as to read --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This, as you will agree, is a form of a decision. Can you read the title of this enactment and paragraph 1, this decision, and what it says below. But please read slowly for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision on assignment to work duty. Item 1: Military conscript or person subject to work duty, Ibrahim Zurapovic from Samac is hereby assigned to work at the DD socially-owned enterprised master from Samac as a metalsmith, as a locksmith."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person before the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you asked the witness to read slowly fine, but before the interpretation was completed you asked the question. Please do pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we have the cite of that again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just want to confirm the cite, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D22F/2 ter. This is a document introduced by my colleague Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have asked my question, but I would like your answer on record. Did you know this person, Ibrahim Zurapovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean Bice [phoen], he worked in Mebos before the war. Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please read in the bottom next to the signature on the left-hand side, it says: "Chief or head," and then there is a name and surname. Could you read that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. That's what it says below the word "head".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you read what it says on the stamp next to that name and surname?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's unclear. It's illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Our case manager just indicated that he believes this document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we confirm with the Registry assistant, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. All the documents running to D22I/2 are under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, in that case, it should be redacted from the public record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read out the first sentence above the signature. Read it aloud, please, but slowly.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I agree with the assignment to work duty, Ministry of Defence, section of Samac."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have no further questions concerning this document. Thank you. Do you know that the work obligation is something that is governed by the law or national defence?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that it is in the immediate purview of the Defence Ministry of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now have a couple of questions relating to the premises on the first floor from where, as you said, orders were coming. And based on that, you made your conclusions as to who organised the work obligation. You did go to the first floor, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The last portion of that question he is adding an argumentative statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner, what is the basis of your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm objecting to that argumentative statement that he said. I have no problem with him saying, I was going to -- I'm going to ask you some more questions on the first floor, concerning the first floor. And based on that you made your conclusions as to who organised the work obligation. That's taking his testimony out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I only quoted from the witness's testimony. He said that all the orders regarding work obligation came from the upper floor. I don't see that this is prolemicising. I don't agree with that, but if you want me, I'll rephrase it. The witness himself put it that way ten minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just ask him to rephrase it. That's not how my view of how the evidence has come out over the past few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, perhaps you can rephrase your question and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do that, Your Honour, but with your leave may I add that the OTP often requires the Defence to indicate the thrust of their cross-examination. And I think I have done precisely that by quoting the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on the first floor of the retirement home, there was an office of the red cross?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that there was a flag of the Red Cross flying on top of that building of the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Sveto Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that he worked in the local Red Cross office?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him about ten times with the request that he put me on the list for exchange, if that's what you call the Red Cross then so be it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that registration for exchange was conducted in the local Red Cross office with Sveto Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the Red Cross office. I know Sveto though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are sure that the Red Cross was not housed on the first floor of that building?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Velo Maslic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maslic, I do know, but the name, first name, Velo means nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Rado Muhinovic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know everybody in Samac, but I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not insist. Do you remember Javanovic Janka?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the first floor, that also local commune premises were on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know, or the premises were not there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The premises were not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was in the offices of the local commune, the one before the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the office of Miroslav Tadic, and to the right Sveto Vasovic, and I would always meet. And when I went up, I would meet Cipo [phoen] and Pero [phoen] Ciko Tesic [phoen] and Pero Torovac [phoen]. These were some older people, and I don't know what was the function of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you go up the floor, how many offices were there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would enter into three offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not my question. I asked, do you remember how many offices there were on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there more than three offices?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been more than three, because it's a big floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you go up the staircase, you enter the hall. You said that straight at the end of the hall, there was Miroslav Tadic's office?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Straight from the staircase, straight the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And next to that office?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sveto, and to the left there would be a glass panel. Pero and the other persons I have mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person going by the name of Zeljko Volasevic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that he was the secretary of the local commune prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he was doing something, that he was working up there, but I didn't know that he was the secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have upstairs his office, or was he upstairs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go -- enter the local commune premises. I don't know whether he had an office there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that you saw him working up there.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he was doing something up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in Volasevic, Zeljko's office, citizens would come who would sign up for firewood to be received via the local commune?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. May I say, Sveto Tesic, Pero Tomorac [phoen], and even who trained and taught driving for the driver's license, they came in September to my home and asked -- they said, "We've come to help you to see how much fuel you need, how many there are at home, and how much coal you will need." I answered that only I and my wife were at home. And he took, "How many tons will you be needing? And just sign that we visited you." I signed that, but he never returned, and there was no coal. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the local commune issued also receipts for issuing firewood and fuel to the families of dead soldiers and to the poorest families in Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the first floor of the retirement home, the civil protection staff headquarters were located?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Miroslav Tadic was the chief of the civil defence, chief of staff of civil protection?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that as far burials and organisation of burials were performed for the entire municipality of Samac by the civil protection staff?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Via Celic, the messenger, I heard that there was a place one could get a coffin and to whom you must turn in order to get a truck. Those were -- that was the information that I received. I didn't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go and ask for the truck of your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Miroslav Tadic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To his office on the first floor in the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier, you said that when you reported for duty assignment in front of the -- you reported in front of the retirement home at 6.00 a.m. in the morning. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not always. But I did come at 6.00 a.m. when I had to come there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, a vehicle would come up -- would come, and you would go for your work assignment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would go on forced labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you would wait there while other groups were taken for their labour assignments?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of this Court, you stated that you were seeing Tadic two to three times a day? I apologise. I believe you stated that you were seeing him two or three times a week in connection with your work assignment.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see him every day when you were receiving your work assignments?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well, maybe he was upstairs; maybe he was not. I would only see him when he was passing by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him at 6.00 in the morning, to be passing by there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to submit and tender another document for the identification. I have only the BHS version, and I must explain to the Trial Chamber that I found this document when we were -- in connection with the exchange of documents of -- reciprocal disclosure. And I would like to say just a few words in connection with this document and discuss it with the witness. I would like to say that this witness, in his statement from 1998, and the statements which were submitted by the Prosecution up until his statement in front of this Chamber, he never stated before that that Miroslav Tadic was the organiser of work assignment. And therefore, I had no reason for considering this document, but I believe this document is -- it has its ERN number, and I have shown this document to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you say that you haven't got the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I only submitted it today for translation. I discovered it only yesterday. This document is open also to the Prosecution, and I submitted to the translation service this document. If it could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to -- only to read that which has been underlined in yellow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you do that, I just want to confirm with the Prosecution whether they are aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, at the break he showed me the document. I have no objection to him using the document. Just his statement that there was no prior indication of Tadic being in a management position or -- I would suggest is not correct, that we keep on talking about three statements. There was never a statement taken from this witness. There is a 1998 interview where he wrote a summary which this witness has never looked at, and there are two other summaries, Prosecution summaries, from this witness. In two and three, there's extensive information concerning Mr. Tadic's role. And I would submit that there also is a lot of information concerning the role in the initial statement in 1998. Other than that, I have no objection. I just want to clarify our view for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. Can we have a number for identification only, because we haven't got the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I state something.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D33/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, may I state something not in connection with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know this cross-examination. He is emphasising one, two, or three statements. I have issued only -- made one statement. If he wants us to talk, we can go out and discuss it among ourselves. I made an official statement here submitted by the gentlemen, and that's all I would have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. You don't have to worry about that. The Prosecution is following the proceedings, and they will always also put on record what, in their view, is the position, and then the Trial Chamber will be able to decide at the end of the proceedings. But any time you feel like saying what you think should be explained, you should say so, and it's all right to have it on record. So do not worry about the status of any statement. Just go ahead and answer the questions put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you only to read that what has been highlighted in yellow. Please read it slowly because nobody has a translation in the courtroom.
