utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I will read that what the Serbian republic, SAO. "The Serbian autonomous region of Sombalian Mijeca [phoen], Municipality of Bosanski Samac, secretariat of economic affairs, number 2533/92." Date: 31 or 21st of the 9th month, 1992. Department -- I can't see the rest. Is it U? NN? "Ministry of National Defence, Bosanski Samac. Subject: Work assignment."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look down at the end of the page, that what has been highlighted.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Secretary of the Secretariat for Economic Affairs".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not make suggestions. Could it be that -- look at the document. Could it be that it's written "the Department of the Ministry of National Defence"?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what -- it's possible that it's the Ministry --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's not what I wanted to ask you. There's another question I would like to ask you. Do you know that various institutions, organisation, would turn to the Ministry of National Defence with a request for the division and the distribution, allocation, of work assignments?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the work assignments were allotted on the first floor of the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you a few questions concerning the people you were mentioning yesterday in your statement and who were then taking you to your work assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Usher, you can use this document. I will not take it any more -- use it [sic].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, you've stated that a person going by the name and nickname of Mile Pancir, that he took you to the trenches?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the transport and digging of trenches, did he mention that he received the orders from Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody dared asked him anything, but no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Stojan Blagojevic. You mentioned that he was always in front of the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he answer that he -- did he say that he received the orders from Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody dared ask anything him either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who you described as Tovirac from Srpska Tisina in picking the harvest, did he mention that he received orders from Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also -- he didn't come. He had this assignment of supplying the military kitchens, and I didn't ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that the drivers, truck drivers, who were taking you, that they received orders from Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mile Pancir never drove a truck, neither Stojan Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will question Skeja.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Skeja was a truck driver. He was driving for a company of Buducnost, but he didn't come in front of the retirement home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Skeja ever say that he received orders from Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Skeja, no. Skeja, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I hear the name now of that truck driver who said that he received orders from Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names, there was a driver who I cannot say either the first name or surname. But prior to -- before the war, he drove that blue -- blue truck, TAM truck. He was a blond person. And there was another one when we were transporting bricks, and they always had to go up and down in order to get their papers from Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slowly, because this is a fact that has to be clarified. If you don't know the name of this person, please give me a close description. We have to determine the truth. Tell me who the person is, where he took you for your assignment. You don't have to say the name and surname.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was of a shorter build, blond. He worked in the past in Ribarska. That was a long time a fish farm. He drove a TAM truck, a green TAM truck. He also would take people for their assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know him well. I cannot remember. He is not a man from Samac but from a village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I need clarification from the witness. When he says he can't mention the names, and you, Counsel, when putting the question to him, also you did say you don't have to name the surname. I want information. I want clarification from the witness. Is it because you cannot remember these drivers' names, or is it because you feel they ought to be protected and cannot have their names mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not protecting, but I just don't know the names. But Mile Pancir was never a driver. The others, these were our supervisors. As far as the drivers are concerned, I cannot remember the names. I know the people, but I cannot remember their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can proceed, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to hear as much data.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember the name, I will tell it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the man was from a village.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was from a Serbian village, from Torsinovac [phoen], I believe. And that is, Serbs lived there

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described that when taking the firewood up to two women who lived above the Mebos shop, you stated yesterday - it's page 49 - and the fourth line of the transcript, that you knew this -- these women personally?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I cannot remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe exactly the building where they lived? Was it the building where the Mebos shop was located? To what floor? This was in the town where you were born.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The second floor, straight one door, and one door was to the left. And that is where the two women. They were office workers in Agropromet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the husband of one of these women died at war, in fighting?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, how much more time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. My colleague's asked me to complete five minutes earlier. But I believe I'll be needing another hour, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's why I am asking, because the Trial Chamber was informed that there are matters to be raised before we rise today. So we can adjourn the cross-examination to tomorrow at 14.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Approximately one hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall adjourn the cross-examination to tomorrow at 14.15 hours. And can the witness be led out of the courtroom while we raise matters that need to be discussed by the Trial Chamber and the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The first item is on the request yesterday by the -- on behalf of the accused persons on the religious holiday of Orthodox Easter. The Trial Chamber communicated to the parties through the registry assistant that it is not possible to grant both days simply because of the delays that the -- these proceedings have faced for problems beyond the control of the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber is very sympathetic to the religious needs of the accused persons, but we felt that we could compromise and perhaps give them one day of the two days, either the Friday or a Monday. And we have been informed that they are agreeable to have a Friday as a non-working day. And the Friday when the Trial Chamber will not sit is the 3rd of May. After Thursday, the proceedings will continue on the 1st of May, which is a Wednesday, and on the 2nd of May, which is a Thursday. And then the Friday, the 3rd May, the Trial Chamber will not sit. The proceedings will continue on the 6th of May onwards as previously scheduled. Any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you very much for this information on behalf of all defendants and my colleagues. In fact, this afternoon, after the second break, the Defence were provided with the witness, well, statement of Mr. Sabrija Dagovic. This is a Mrs. Sabrija Dagovic. And this statement was made and done in 1995, actually on the 9th of May in 1995, which means almost seven years ago. In spite of all our efforts as a Defence to follow the proceedings and to establish a certain principle of fairness in this trial, the Prosecution, I must say, acted in a manner of gross and blatant violation of this trial and the principles of fairness of trial. We asked on many occasions that our friends from Prosecution discover all relevant materials to the Defence, to disclose. In spite of all our efforts, and in spite of the instructions of this Honourable Trial Chambers to the Prosecution, and certain, I would say, warnings, here we are in the situation today that we were provided with this particular statement from 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm wondering, where is the end of this intolerable practice and how the impact and the effect on this trial proceeding would be? I must say that we are going into the area where we shall raise the issue regarding the possible miscarriage of justice due to these kinds of actions from our colleagues of the Prosecution. So I kindly ask this Trial Chamber to take necessary measures, including sanctions which are provided in our Rules of Procedure, in order to stop this practice, and also in order to take this note with regard to the possible impact of the fairness of these trial proceedings. Thank you very much for your attention, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you sit down, you said it's Mrs. Sabrija Dagovic because I see on the list of witnesses provided by the Prosecution, there is a Safet Dagovic. Is that the spouse? Do you know whether it is the spouse?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have no idea. Mr. Weiner, I'll call upon you. You have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is the father of two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one and which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Safet and Esad Dagovic. One of these two witnesses was here before this Trial Chamber, and the other will come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. That statement which has been given to you today by the Prosecution is the statement of the father of Safet Dagovic, who is listed as a witness yet to come, and Esad Dagovic who has already given evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Pantelic, whether the maker of that statement is also coming as a witness? Do you know? Is he not on the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe that this person will not come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. He is on the list of witnesses provided to you by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, he is not on the list. Because this statement was discovered to the Defence in accordance with Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it was given to the Defence today, as you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has never been on our witness list. This witness is not going to be on our witness list. One of this witness's sons has already testified, and the other one is scheduled to testify. We provided this to counsel as a potentially Rule 68 document. We continue to look through and look through our records. We continue to look through documents as they come along. If we see anything which is discoverable under Rule 68, we immediately provide it to Defence counsel. This is not something -- this is not something that has been a blatant violation, as counsel indicated. Things happen. In fact, today, the last document which was introduced was just shown to us moments ago. There isn't even a translation of it. The last document that was shown to that witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. I'm not asking you to discuss the other document because you didn't discuss it then when it arose. I did ask you about it. The point is, that document has been in the Office of the Prosecutor since 1995 when it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which is long before any of the three of our counsel have been here. We've continued to look through the records. If we find anything, we immediately turn it over to Defence counsel, which is our obligation. This is not a witness that is going to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not the point. We understand that's your obligation. But why wasn't it discovered long before today? Because it has been with the Prosecutor's office since 1995. It's not a question of you deciding whether or not he is going to be a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There are approximately 2 and a half -- or over 2 and a half million documents in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor. As we continue to look through, it is not always as easy because of names are spelled incorrectly. Some names are in Cyrillic. Some names have the accents. So when you do name checks, we don't always find the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That document is -- in what language is it, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the English language, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it's not in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy would like to comment on it. She is the one who found the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I explain. The statement to which Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Pantelic has spoken is the statement of Sabrija Dagovic who, we understand, is indeed the father of Esad and Safet. In the statement of Sabrija Dagovic, there is no mention of his sons' names or anything like that. So when this was looked through, there was no way we would know that was actually the father or, in fact, a relation to these other people. I think you are aware there are many --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just explaining. That's why I think in the initial thing, it was never connected. Over the break, we have gone through every single statement of every person we have spoken to in relation to this case. And in that review, this document was reread again, and there is one sentence in it which is potentially Rule 68. On discovering that and knowing that Mr. Safet Dagovic is the next witness up, we immediately disclose it as potentially Rule 68. The Defence will have an opportunity to put any questions they think that arise from the statement to Mr. Dagovic. And I think that Mr. Pantelic, instead of making these repeated statements about blatant violations, should be very concrete in exactly the prejudice that is shown. It is simply for that reason --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- because it's not blatantly obvious from it it is a Rule 68 document because the names of the witnesses and that do not appear on the face of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it your position that it's not discussing any of the defendants' involvement?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No. What it does is it discusses this -- a witness of the Prosecution, his son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: My question is clear: Is that document discussing any of the defendants' involvement in the allegations in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, not in any exculpatory manner, but I don't think -- I think the names may be mentioned, but I don't think -- there is certainly nothing -- in fact, that's why he wasn't called as a witness. He basically has nothing to say about the defendants; he only has something to say about his sons. And I think it's in that context that once we put two and two together, we thought it could potentially be a Rule 68 relating to our witnesses, not about any exculpatory acts on behalf of any of the defendants in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you hold on, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you hold on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a question to the Prosecution. What is the relevance of that document for this trial? Why should it be put forward, communicated to the Defence, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason that we communicated it to the Defence is that the statement giver is the father of two witnesses, and indeed, the next witness. And the Defence may wish to read it and then to use it as a basis for their cross-examination of the next witness. To that extent, it's -- in a broad reading of exculpatory information, it could be useful to the Defence, in fact, under the rules of reciprocal discovery here, which don't apply to Mr. Pantelic, but as potentially under Rule 68. So it could be useful in the cross-examination of the next witness, but not pointing to any direct exculpatory behaviour or mitigating factors on the part of the Defence -- any of the defendants. And it was in that context that it was communicated to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If I may continue, you said that that document may be useful for the Defence. Listening to Defence Counsel Pantelic, it sounds rather that he views it as a possible miscarriage of justice. So that is some kind of -- you are not in harmony with each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. And I think -- the other position of the Prosecution would be that it is for Mr. Pantelic, if he is raising a very serious allegation and he is asking the Trial Chamber to take quite serious measures that he has alluded to, that we have been in blatant violation, that it should be for him to specify very clearly and very concretely why he thinks this is such a miscarriage of justice. Because I think that the general tone and manner of which Mr. Pantelic has put his complaint on the record is not of particular assistance in being able to make a factual determination. And we are happy to address this in writing or to reply to Mr. Pantelic if he can be very specific and justify his complaint to the Tribunal -- to the Chamber. We are in no doubt that -- we apologise that this has been disclosed now. We wanted to disclose it before Safet Dagovic came up. We have no problem with disclosing it and doing so as a matter of caution. But we would reject any of these allegations that Mr. Pantelic has made about our practice, et cetera, which is not the first time in these proceedings that he has attempted to put such, I would, say unfounded allegations on to the record. But perhaps if he was concrete in exactly the nature of the miscarriage of justice that has been performed by the late disclosure of this document, we would be in a better position to respond and assist the Bench and Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the Trial Chamber would like to deal with this matter fully, and the Trial Chamber will adjourn -- you'll be given your opportunity tomorrow to respond, because we don't want to go over the limits for the interpreters and also the accused persons. The Defence will be able to respond fully tomorrow. We'll decide -- before the witness comes in, so that we deal with it. And if the Bench has any questions, the matter will be dealt with then. If there are any other matters that the counsel wish to have on record, let's deal with that tomorrow before the witness is brought in to the courtroom at 14.15. We shall adjourn until tomorrow at 14.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of April, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
